area: Procedural vector rendering performance (Phaser 3.90 Graphics vs pre-rendered textures)

item_verdicts.title: Pre-rendering the ~40 transcribed animation frames to textures
item_verdicts.why: Both docs quotes verified verbatim on the live page ('decomposed into polygons... expensive processes, especially with complex shapes'; generateTexture 'bake' remedy). Discourse 11026 verified: iOS perf collapse traced to WebKit bug 230749, not Graphics. Frame count is exactly 40 (20 walk + 4 + 9 + 7, machine-counted in config/ogAnims.ts). Repo claims check out: drawFighters runs composePose->planPose->drawPlan into one cleared this.fx Graphics every update; RESUME_HERE line 56 says '57 files / 894 tests green'; no perf deficit documented anywhere. One unrefuted-but-soft spot: the implementation_note's ruling that runtime baking 'does NOT violate' src/game/CLAUDE.md is its own legal reading — the invariant says 'All art is procedural vector (Graphics)', and a sprite render path is arguably a spirit violation needing an owner call; MEASURE_FIRST plus the hazard-rider item already gate this, so the adjudication survives.

item_verdicts.title: Exact profiling protocol before any rendering change
item_verdicts.why: The protocol and ADOPT adjudication survive: main.ts lines 79-117 verified — ?fidelity=auto self-runs the gate and parks a verdict in localStorage (harness exported from src/game/fidelity.ts), and the discourse thread genuinely recommends 'using spector js to investigate draw call and frame buffer'. But the '~60 calls on a Phaser 3.24 tilemap' measurement appears in NEITHER cited source: discourse 11026 contains no such number (fetched and checked explicitly), and the generalistprogrammer guide never mentions Spector.js at all — so its C-grade citation titled 'draw-call counting with Spector.js' does not support what it is cited for.
item_verdicts.correction: Drop the '~60 calls on a Phaser 3.24 tilemap' anecdote (found in no cited source) and drop/relabel the generalistprogrammer citation (page exists but never mentions Spector.js). Keep Spector.js on the strength of discourse 11026 alone. Also: the ?fidelity=auto + localStorage wiring lives in src/main.ts, not src/game/fidelity.ts (which exports the harness).

item_verdicts.title: Plan cache keyed by (anim, frameIndex, mirrored) - remove the 60Hz recompute of a 15fps pose
item_verdicts.why: Core mechanism verified against the repo: ANIM_TIMING.poseStepMs = 1000/15 (config/anim.ts:106); drawPlan calls Phaser.Geom.Polygon.Earcut per holedFill op every frame (OgArtScene.ts:135); toStagePoints in artPlan.ts bakes the stage origin into every point, so the cache does require the origin-at-(0,0) refactor claimed; tests/a11Mirror.test.ts exists. I attacked the memo key via the carry-forward contract and it SURVIVED: all four anims open with full 19-node frames (machine-counted), and partc's sparse frames (19,0,19,0,19,19,7) apply sequentially from frame 0, so (anim, frameIndex, mirrored) does fully determine the pose. But the claim overstates the idle case: when idle, composePose is NOT recomputed — DuelScene.fighterPose returns this.fighterParts/fighterPartsMirrored composed ONCE in create(); only planPose + Earcut run redundantly at 60Hz while idle.
item_verdicts.correction: composePose is already cached for the idle pose (composed once in create(), both facings); the 60Hz composePose recompute happens only while walking or slashing. The always-on 60Hz redundancy is planPose + Earcut (drawPlan), which run every frame in every state. Frame count is exactly 40 transcribed frames (not ~45), so the cache is ~41 keys x 2 facings including the static dressed idle.

item_verdicts.title: Texture baking is a pixel-fidelity hazard on this stack (WebGL1 no-AA framebuffers, DPR blur)
item_verdicts.why: Hazard (1) is rock solid: the DynamicTexture docs page carries the exact sentence 'Under WebGL1, a FrameBuffer, which is what this Dynamic Texture uses internally, cannot be anti-aliased.' Repo machinery verified: captureArea in OgArtScene.ts, core/inkBox.ts exists, fidelity 55/55 confirmed in RESUME_HERE. Hazard (2) is overstated: issue #4408 is real and says what is claimed, but it is CLOSED and 3.15-era — the issue itself notes Phaser 3.16.1/3.16.2 hardcoded resolution to 1, so the 'resolution != 1' blur path cannot occur on the pinned phaser@3 stack as described. The item's adjudication survives on hazard (1) alone.
item_verdicts.correction: Rest the hazard on the WebGL1 no-AA docs sentence alone. Reframe #4408 as historical evidence that framebuffer output and DPR interact badly, not a live trap: since Phaser 3.16 the resolution config is hardcoded to 1, so 'blurry whenever game resolution != 1' cannot manifest on phaser@3 today. Keep the practical advice (bake at devicePixelRatio-scaled size, rerun the 55/55 gate + owner LOOK).

item_verdicts.title: Draw-call batching by grouping Graphics work
item_verdicts.why: Docs quote verified verbatim ('Under WebGL, Graphics uses its own shader which will batch drawing operations... Avoid mixing object types where possible, as each batch will be flushed'). ALREADY_DONE verified line-by-line in DuelScene.ts: strokes, trails, droplets, both fighters (drawPlan), kunai, and kill-beat flash all draw into the single this.fx (depth 10); all HUD chrome into the single this.hud (depth 20); every Text sits at depth 21-22; the arena is a third Graphics drawn once in create() at default depth; the only objects between bands are non-rendering Zones. Depth bands arena < fx < hud < texts hold exactly as claimed. The '~16 textures per draw call' parenthetical is unverified (the cited phaser.io tutorial is CE-era) but non-load-bearing to the verdict.

overall_note: Research output is substantially honest: 5 of 6 distinct cited URLs fetched — all live, and both A-grade Phaser docs quotes are verbatim-exact, which is the load-bearing evidence for items 1, 3, 4, and 5. The one fabrication-shaped detail found is the '~60 draw calls on a Phaser 3.24 tilemap' anecdote, present in neither source cited for it (item 2 weakened, not killed). Repo readings were accurate except one: the claim that composePose recomputes at 60Hz 'when idle' — the idle pose is composed once in create(); the genuine always-on 60Hz waste is planPose + Earcut. Ledger check: no cited row is overturned — §00b corrects f-8/f-9/e-7/a-6 (none relied on here) and §S24-H corrects a-2/a-5/gap-G/gap-H (also not relied on); the 15fps latch survives as the committed repo contract (ANIM_TIMING.poseStepMs), though §00 notes 15fps is the CAPTURE's sampling floor and the original game likely ran 24-30fps — irrelevant to the cache math, which keys off our own latch. The adversarial attack on the plan-cache memo key failed: all four anims open with full 19-node frames, so (anim, frameIndex, mirrored) fully determines the pose despite the carry-forward contract.
